red_flags: Any lump larger than 5 cm, deep to the fascia, hard, fixed, or rapidly growing — soft-tissue sarcoma until proven otherwise; urgent surgical referral
Recurrence at the site of a previously excised lump
Rapidly spreading redness with fever and severe pain around a lump — deep infection
A 'lipoma' that has become painful and started growing
Enlarging lump with unexplained weight loss
exam: Measure the lump and record the exact site — a diagram or measurement makes growth objective at review
Assess consistency: soft (lipoma), firm and rubbery (node), tense cystic (cyst/ganglion), stony hard (malignancy)
Test attachment to skin — a cyst is attached to skin, often with a visible punctum; a lipoma is free beneath it
Test the slip sign — edges slipping away from the finger support lipoma
Contract the underlying muscle — a lump that becomes fixed or disappears is deep to fascia (raises sarcoma stakes)
Test fluctuation and transillumination — cystic lesions fluctuate; a ganglion transilluminates weakly, a lipoma may glow softly
Percuss or tap the lump for paresthesia along a nerve — supports neurofibroma/nerve-sheath origin
Look for redness, warmth, and pointing — abscess
Palpate the regional lymph nodes draining the site
Survey the rest of the skin — multiple lipomas, café-au-lait patches and axillary freckling (neurofibromatosis), or a pigmented dimpling nodule (dermatofibroma)

investigations.why: First-line: tells cystic (ganglion, abscess) from solid (lipoma, node, sarcoma), measures true size, and shows the critical fact of depth relative to fascia
Leukocytosis and raised CRP support abscess or infected cyst over the sterile lumps
Recurrent skin abscesses or carbuncles are often the presentation of undiagnosed diabetes

investigations.test: FNAC of a suspected lymph node
investigations.why: Separates reactive node from tuberculous and neoplastic nodes when the 'soft-tissue lump' turns out to be nodal
Shows calcification, a bony origin, or pressure changes — separates a bony swelling from a soft-tissue one near joints
Second-line — mandatory before any biopsy if the lump is >5 cm, deep, or suspicious on ultrasound: characterizes and stages a possible sarcoma for the referral center
